meta.siteTitle: Indigenous Peoples of Quebec — The 11 First Nations
meta.siteDescription: History, culture and languages of the 11 Indigenous nations and Inuit of Quebec.

home.heroSub: An in-depth article series on the First Nations and Inuit who have lived on Quebec territory for millennia.
home.introTitle: A history that begins long before Quebec
home.introP1: Long before Jacques Cartier reached the St. Lawrence in 1534, dozens of Indigenous nations had lived on this territory for millennia. Hunters, farmers, navigators, diplomats — each people developed a unique civilization, rooted in the land and passed down through extraordinarily rich oral traditions.
home.introP2: This series invites you to discover the 11 First Nations and the Inuit of Nunavik — their history, culture, traditions and place in Quebec today. An invitation to respect and understanding.
home.nationsSub: Click a nation to read its article
home.serieSub: 8 series of ten articles (#1 to #80): spirituality, history, Quebec know-how, forgotten wisdom, living culture… Each card opens the full article.
home.serieNotice: All articles in one place. Series 1 (#1–#10) to Series 8 (#71–#80) — listen button (▶ Listen) on each page.
home.carnetsDesc: Tales of a coureur des bois across Quebec's 11 First Nations — hunting, fishing, fire, winter, portages. 5 notebooks published. Read-aloud · EN / ES.
home.communityP: Share these articles, discuss, and learn more about Indigenous peoples in Quebec. Join our Facebook group or visit the series website.

below.lang1Body: Cree, Innu, Atikamekw, Mi'kmaq — millennia-old languages threatened with extinction. Communities bringing them back to life despite residential school legacies and pressures of cultural assimilation.
below.lang2Body: Nine Indigenous languages survive in Quebec — some on the edge of extinction. Discover how First Nations revitalize them through school immersion, digital resources and intergenerational transmission.
below.womenBody: Long before Europeans arrived, Indigenous women governed, decided and transmitted knowledge. Among the Wendat and Mohawks, they named chiefs and could remove them. Colonization tried to erase this power — they are reclaiming it.
below.womenCap1: Wendat council — Clan Mothers appointed chiefs
below.womenCap2: Fight for missing and murdered women — MMIWG
below.womenCap3: Elders — keepers of knowledge and memory
below.a58Title: Indigenous Fishing — Nets, Traps and River Knowledge
below.a58Body: First Nations developed sophisticated, sustainable fishing techniques using nets and traps. Discover how Indigenous peoples mastered Quebec's waters before colonization.
below.a71Title: #71 — Sacred Ceremonies of the Indigenous Peoples of Quebec
below.a71Body: Pow-wow, sacred drum, sweat lodge, vision quest, rites of passage… Explore the spiritual life of Quebec's 11 nations — and their renewal today.
below.a71Cap1: The sacred drum — heart of spiritual life
below.a71Cap2: Sweat lodge — purification of body and soul
below.a71Cap3: Transmission — the challenge of the century
below.jewelTitle: The Art of First Nations Jewelry
below.jewelBody: Wampum, porcupine quills, silver and ivory — discover how Quebec's 11 nations transformed the territory's resources into works of profound beauty and meaning.
below.quoteText: “These peoples do not belong to the past. They are alive, present, and their future is being built now — on the same territories they never left.”
below.footerDesc: This article series was produced with respect for each nation presented. It aims to share their remarkable history with Quebec and international audiences.
below.footerCopy: FAQ · Series produced with Lucie · Educational content · 2026

carnetsPage.metaTitle: Pierre le Fouineur's Notebooks — First Nations of Quebec
carnetsPage.title: 📜 Pierre le Fouineur's Notebooks
carnetsPage.intro: Stories left by my friend Pierre's great-grandfather — coureur des bois, trade with First Nations, a treasury of knowledge about Quebec's eleven nations. I pass them on as written, inventing nothing.
carnetsPage.portrait: Pierre le Fouineur — coureur des bois in Quebec. He walked the portages, listened to the Elders, wrote at night in leather notebooks. Each notebook explores one skill: hunting, fishing, fire, winter, portages… An old text, shared with respect.
